motivation: Full dated notice plus retrieval matched chronological replay on all 16 judged factual outcomes. A costly repair of the 1,968 skipped later positions did not add answers. Try reducing the amount of the incoming dialogue that must enter the large model's cache. Keep a short extract of complete original turns before any question arrives.
candidate: Use the first three recurrent layers of the frozen 4-bit Qwen3.5-9B model. Collect four query vectors per shared head at the fixed generic chat-template suffix. For each arriving turn, compare the layer-2 terminal recurrent state with its value writes muted over that turn while keys, erase gates, decay gates and previous state are fixed. Score the turn by the mean change in headwise RMS-normalized reads across the fixed probes and heads. Replay original selected turns in chronological order as a dated update. Normalize neither by future question nor gold importance. Use score divided by square root of the turn's token length in the budgeted ranking. Include a pre-normalization raw-read comparator with otherwise identical processing.
data: All distinct arriving sessions among the 23 metadata-eligible delayed-session pairs from the first four development users of HaluMem-Medium. Score every unique official Dynamic Update question in those pairs. Selection receives only the raw delayed session and the last 128 tokens preceding it; historical user names and dates come from genuine turns. Neither official questions, references nor memory-point annotations enter the selector. Keep every case in summaries and report the attainable subset whose actual delayed session contains the normalized contiguous reference phrase. This proxy cannot establish answer accuracy.
baselines: At most 25% of the original token cost per session using complete turns, packed greedily in priority order until none fit. Compare latest turns first, uniform temporal coverage, user turns first with recency ties, mean within-session IDF divided by square-root length, dense Contriever similarity to the session centroid divided by square-root length, raw write-induced read displacement and the normalized method. Use identical dated source text, tokenization and whole-turn budget. The neural notice will receive the full text in the later QA stage. No answer-conditioned prompt compression.
decision: Advance to a genuine two-turn 9B service only if (a) at least eight changed questions across at least three users have a literal source witness, (b) the normalized method retains at least 80% of those eligible questions, and (c) it retains at least two more grounded answers than each simple text or semantic control and at least one more than unnormalized read displacement at the same budget. Report paired gains/losses and every denominator. If the screen fails, discard this selective-write rule without using any held-out user or claiming a lower serving cost.
limits: Local machine, no paid credits. Up to 15 minutes for the evidence-retention screen and one implementation repair. Time select/encode components independently; no end-to-end timing or novel compression claim at this stage.
